hints: Remember the question asks about the reverse reaction, not the forward one, so flip your thinking to making $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ from $\text{SO}_3$.
Count the gas moles: 3 moles on the left ($2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2$) versus 2 moles on the right ($2\text{SO}_3$), so think which pressure pushes equilibrium to the side with more moles.
The forward $\Delta H$ is negative (exothermic), so the reverse is endothermic, now ask yourself which temperature favours an endothermic change.
walkthrough:
**Spot what forward and reverse mean**

Think of this like a tug of war. Forward makes $\text{SO}_3$, reverse breaks $\text{SO}_3$ back down.

$$2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3 \quad \Delta H^o = -196 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Use pressure to favour more gas moles**

Le Chatelier says high pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles, low pressure favours the side with more gas moles. Forward goes from 3 to 2 moles, so forward likes high pressure.

$$\text{reverse: 2 moles} \rightarrow \text{3 moles, so low pressure favours reverse}$$

**Use temperature to favour the endothermic direction**

Forward is exothermic ($\Delta H$ negative, gives out heat). Reverse must therefore be endothermic (takes in heat). High temperature always favours the endothermic direction.

$$\text{reverse is endothermic, so high temperature favours reverse}$$

**Combine both conditions**

Low pressure pushes to more moles (reverse). High temperature pushes to endothermic (reverse). Together they both favour the reverse reaction.

options.A: High pressure favours the forward reaction (3 to 2 moles), not the reverse. High temperature does favour reverse, but the pressure part is wrong, so this is only half correct.
options.B: This is the classic trap. High pressure and low temperature favour the forward reaction to make $\text{SO}_3$ (Contact process conditions). The question asks for the reverse, which is the exact opposite.
options.C: Low pressure favours the side with more gas moles, which is the left side (3 moles vs 2 moles). High temperature favours the endothermic direction, which is the reverse. Both conditions push equilibrium to the left.
options.D: Low pressure does favour reverse, but low temperature favours the exothermic forward reaction. The temperature part is wrong here, so equilibrium would be pulled in opposite directions.
